subject: Re: DocSuite discovery — model-fit deep dive & prompt harvest
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Smith <jared@docsuite.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: DocSuite discovery — model fit & prompt harvest

Thanks again for the conversation today, Jared — helpful to walk through your primary flows (document ingestion -> search + Q&A -> triage/summary). Quick recap and concrete asks so we can scope the eval/POC: 

Recap (short):
- Primary success metric: reduce time-to-resolution for support cases by 40% while keeping extractive answer recall >92%.
- Sensitive content: customer PII and internal case notes flagged as sensitive; redaction and audit log retention will be required.
- Expected throughput: 50 concurrent users, ~200 tokens/request avg for interactive flows; batch exports (nightly) of ~5k docs/day.

Initial model recommendations (for eval):
- Redwood-RT-Large (8-bit quant + KV caching) — best latency/cost balance for interactive Q&A.
- Llama2-13B-q4 (open baseline) — for comparison on hallucination/recall.
- Fallback small model: Redmini-6B (cheap fallback for low-priority queries).

Benchmarks & materials: I’ve attached a prompt sample template and our redaction checklist for PII. Please share: 200–300 representative prompts/calls (can be anonymized), and flag ~20 edge-case queries that are high-risk for hallucinations (legal language, temporal reasoning, ambiguous pronouns).

Action items / ask from DocSuite:
1) Share a zipped CSV of prompt samples using attached template (prompt_sample_template.csv) — include user intent label where possible.
2) Mark any prompts that contain PII or require redaction — include examples of how you’d prefer redaction to work.
3) Note any hard safety guardrails (e.g., NEVER summarize flagged financial disclosures).
4) Confirm timeline: can you get samples by EOD next Tue (2028-03-12)?

We’ll:
- Stand up a small eval with Redwood-RT-Large and Llama2-13B-q4 and run the provided prompt bank through our eval harness (quality/regression metrics + latency/cost).
- Share a public benchmark link for DocSuite’s test set and an initial model recommendation within 5 business days after we receive the prompts.

Attachments: prompt_sample_template.csv (text/csv), redaction_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa and Mina to coordinate the evaluation plan and sample intake.

—
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

From: Jared Smith <jared@docsuite.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 09:03:22 -0800
Subject: Re: DocSuite discovery — model fit & prompt harvest

Appreciate the recap, Mateo — this aligns with our notes. A couple quick clarifications before we assemble samples: 

1) On redaction: We currently mask customer PII at ingest but retain a hashed identifier for linking. For the eval, do you want fully redacted (replace with [REDACTED]) or synthetic replacements?
2) For the 20 edge cases, do you want them as separate rows with context (chat transcript + doc snippet) or just the prompt itself?

We’ll aim to get you a first batch by Tue next week — procurement is also asking about the cost model for dedicated capacity if the POC looks good. Looping procurement at procurement@docsuite.ai.

Thanks,
Jared
Head of Product | DocSuite
Jared.Smith@docsuite.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 10:15:07 -0700
Subject: Re: DocSuite discovery — model fit & prompt harvest

Great questions, Jared — Marissa here (solutions engineering). Short answers and proposed format below.

Redaction preference:
- For eval purposes we prefer fully redacted examples (replace PII with [REDACTED]) plus one synthetic-replacement example if you’re comfortable. This lets us measure model behavior without leaking anything.

Format for edge cases:
- Please provide edge cases as separate rows in the attached CSV with these columns: prompt_text, context_snippet, expected_behavior (accept/flag/decline), sensitivity_label (PII/Confidential/None). Context_snippet can be up to 512 chars.

What we’ll deliver after samples:
- A shared benchmark report (link below) with per-model precision/recall for extractive answers, hallucination rate, and latency/cost per 1k tokens.
- Recommendations: likely Redwood-RT-Large for interactive flows; we’ll also include quantization notes and caching config to hit your latency SLOs.

Logistics & timeline
- If you can drop a Drive folder or a zipped CSV by EOD Tue 2028-03-12, we’ll start the eval the same day. Initial results and a short deck by Fri 2028-03-16.

HubSpot: I’ve attached the templated CSV (prompt_sample_template.csv) and our redaction checklist (redaction_checklist.pdf). For tracking, I’ll add these files to deal DS-2028-1452 in HubSpot.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0222

Thanks, Marissa — that format makes sense. I created a shared Drive folder and uploaded an initial 120-row CSV plus a folder named "edge-cases" with 22 examples. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDocsuitePromptSamples

We redacted PII with [REDACTED] per your checklist and included one synthetic replacement example in the "synthetic" subfolder. Procurement will also follow up with a short questionnaire about Dedicated capacity pricing — procurement@docsuite.ai will send that over today.

We expect to add another ~100 prompts by next Monday (3/13). Thanks, looking forward to the benchmark.

—
Jared Smith
